title: Logical Connectors in Written Discourse
tagline: Year 3 — Words that signal addition, contrast, cause, result, condition and sequence between ideas

introduction.overview: Connectors (however, therefore, although, unless, moreover) tell the reader how two ideas are related. The same two clauses can say different things depending on the connector: adding, contrasting, giving a reason, giving a result, or setting a condition. Questions ask you to supply the connector that makes the relationship logical. The method is to name the relationship first, then pick the word that expresses it.
introduction.placementRelevance: Connector questions are common in the verbal sections of company tests and also guide para jumbles and completions.
introduction.realWorldContext: Choosing the right connector decides whether an email reads as logical or confused.

learningObjectives: Classify relationships: addition, contrast, cause, result, condition, time
Distinguish conjunctions from sentence adverbs and prepositions
Handle paired connectors (not only… but also; neither… nor)
Use punctuation as a clue (semicolon + however)

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A relationship comes first, the word second. Ask: do these two ideas agree, oppose, explain or follow?

coreDefinitions: Contrast: however, nevertheless, although, whereas, on the other hand, in contrast.
Cause: because, since, as, due to, because of.
Result: therefore, consequently, as a result, hence.
Condition: if, unless, provided that, otherwise.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The connector is a road sign. It tells you whether the next idea continues in the same direction, turns against it, explains it or follows from it.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Name the relationship between the two parts. Then choose the connector of that type, and check grammar: after "although" a clause, after "despite" a noun.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Condition
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Unless = if not; otherwise = or else

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Pairs
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Not only… but also; neither… nor; hardly… when

mainNarrative: "The roads were flooded; ______, the schools remained closed." The second idea is the result of the first, so the connector is therefore (a result word).
"She was tired; ______, she finished the report." The second idea goes against what tiredness would suggest, so the connector is nevertheless (contrast).
"______ his illness, he attended the meeting." After a connector that introduces a noun phrase, use despite. "Because of" would give a reason, but the sentence shows contrast.
"You will not pass ______ you study seriously." The meaning is "if you do not study seriously", so unless is correct.
Pairs are fixed: not only… but also; neither… nor; hardly… when; no sooner… than. Choose the second part to match the first.

deepDiveAspects.title: Conjunction vs adverb
deepDiveAspects.content: Although joins clauses in one sentence; however starts a new clause after a semicolon or full stop.

deepDiveAspects.title: Preposition vs conjunction
deepDiveAspects.content: Despite and because of take nouns; although and because take clauses.

solvedExamples.title: Result
solvedExamples.question: The roads were flooded; ______, the schools remained closed. Which connector fits?

steps.title: Relationship
steps.explanation: The second idea is the result of the first.

solvedExamples.title: Noun vs clause
solvedExamples.question: ______ his illness, he attended the meeting. Despite or Although?

solvedExamples.title: Condition
solvedExamples.question: You will not pass ______ you study seriously. Which connector fits?

steps.title: Meaning
steps.explanation: If you do not study seriously, you will not pass.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Name the relationship (add, contrast, cause, result, condition), then choose the connector of that type that fits the grammar.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a result word for a contrast

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate connectors of the wrong type first.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Read the sentence without the blank to find the relationship.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Punctuation hints: a semicolon often precedes however or therefore.

easy.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

The roads were flooded; ______, the schools remained closed.

Which option is correct?
easy.explanation: The closing of the schools is the result of the flooding, so a result connector fits.

easy.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

She was tired; ______, she finished the report.

Which option is correct?
easy.explanation: Finishing the report goes against what tiredness would suggest, so a contrast connector fits.

easy.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

______ it was raining, the match went ahead.

Which option is correct?
easy.explanation: The match going ahead contrasts with the rain, so a concession connector fits.

intermediate.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

Ravi is outgoing, ______ his brother is shy.

Which option is correct?
intermediate.explanation: The two ideas are set against each other, so a contrast conjunction fits.

intermediate.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

Take an umbrella; ______, you may get wet.

Which option is correct?
intermediate.explanation: "Otherwise" means "if you do not", which explains the consequence of not taking an umbrella.

intermediate.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

______ his illness, he attended the meeting.

Which option is correct?
intermediate.explanation: Attending the meeting contrasts with being ill, and a noun phrase follows, so despite fits.

advanced.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

______ the team played well, they lost the match; ______, they did not lose heart.

Which option is correct?
advanced.explanation: Playing well and losing contrast (although); not losing heart despite the loss is another contrast (nevertheless).

advanced.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

The price was low; ______, the quality was poor. ______, customers bought it in large numbers.

Which option is correct?
advanced.explanation: Low price against poor quality is a contrast (however); buying in large numbers despite poor quality is another contrast (nevertheless).

placementStyle.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

He is not only intelligent ______ also hardworking.

Which option is correct?
placementStyle.explanation: "Not only… but also" is a fixed pair.

placementStyle.question:
Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

Neither the manager ______ the clerks knew about the change.

Which option is correct?

Choose the connector (or pair of connectors) that best fills the blank(s).

______ you apologise, she will not speak to you.

Which option is correct?
placementStyle.explanation: The meaning is "if you do not apologise, she will not speak to you".

selfCheckQuestions: Can I tell cause from result?
Can I choose despite or although?
